summary: A 1936 CCC-era lookout house on the Prescott National Forest, no longer in service, reached only by a rigorous hike of about an hour.

facts.design: L-5 groundhouse per NHLR; NRHP record lists the Civilian Conservation Corps as architect

access.note: No road access to the lookout; visitors hike about an hour from the trailhead. The register says the building is no longer in service.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead is 43 miles from Prescott, 18 of them dirt road. The route climbs from about 5,800 ft to the lookout at 7,270 ft. The 2020 visitor found the trail rigorous. No NHLR sign or direction sign at the trailhead.

events.note: L-5 groundhouse constructed (NHLR). NRHP significant year 1936, with CCC listed as architect. A March 1937 newspaper item still described the lookout as yet to be built.
May 1938: a ranger placed Wayne Black as lookout on the point (newspaper item quoted by westlookouts). Earliest staffing named in the sources.
National Register record dated January 28, 1988 (NPGallery 'Date Published'; NRIS 87002491). The record gives no separate listing date.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 5, 2003
Visit report, May 8, 2020: good condition, glass intact, needs paint, screen door needs work, not staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and NRHP record give 1936, but a March 2, 1937 newspaper item describes the lookout as one that will be built soon. The story reports 1936 as the register date and notes the 1937 account.

The NHLR says there is no road access. The trail guide says the trailhead is reached over 18 miles of dirt road from Prescott. Both hold: a road reaches the trailhead, and the last stretch to the lookout is a hike.

notes_for_editor: Date conflict unresolved: register and NRHP say 1936; a March 1937 newspaper item says the lookout will be built soon. Design conflict unresolved: NHLR says L-5 groundhouse. A Living New Deal page (HTTP 403 here, so not verified) reportedly says L-4, and the NRHP nomination PDF is scanned with only its cover in the text layer, so its body could not be checked. The westlookouts items are transcriptions of the Prescott Evening Courier, not the paper itself. The 2020 visit report is a volunteer report, not an official inspection.
